title: Hierarchical Neural Constructive Solver for Real-world TSP Scenarios

problem.claim: Realistic TSP solving requires models that account for local node proximity and efficiently represent unvisited nodes.

gap.claim: Existing neural constructive routing solvers have mainly been evaluated on random instances that inadequately represent real-world scenarios.

contributions.claim: A learnable choice layer prioritizes candidate nodes according to the current location.
A learnable approximate clustering algorithm groups unvisited cities.
The two components form a hierarchical solver combining local neighborhoods with intermediate node representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance against classical and recent transformer models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior neural constructive routing solvers predominantly use transformer-based set-to-sequence formulations.
Their reported efficacy has primarily been shown on random instances that do not adequately capture real-world scenarios.
The paper identifies local proximity and compact tracking of unvisited nodes as important for realistic TSP solving.
It implements these insights through a location-aware choice layer and learnable approximate clustering within a hierarchical solver.
The authors report superior performance relative to classical and recent transformer models.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the industrial scenarios or dataset composition.
Quantitative performance gains and evaluation metrics are omitted.
Training details, clustering implementation details, and computational costs are omitted.
The abstract does not establish generalization beyond the evaluated realistic TSP settings.
